**Answer**

Yes. A salaried employee is entitled to claim a **standard deduction** under **Section 16(ia)** of the Income‑Tax Act.

**Legal basis**

| Provision | What it says | Relevance |
|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| **Section 16(ia) – amendment** | “A deduction of **fifty thousand rupees** or the amount of the salary, whichever is less, shall be made before computing the income under the head ‘Salaries’.” The amendment is effective from 1 Oct 2024. | Confirms that a standard deduction is available to salaried persons and fixes the amount for FY 2024‑25. [C3] |
| **Form‑16 instruction** | The field “Standard Deduction u/s 16(ia)” must be entered as per Part B of Form 16. | Shows that the deduction is to be claimed by salaried employees in their returns. [C5] |
| **New‑tax‑regime rule** | “In case of New Tax Regime, taxpayer being an employee can claim Standard deduction u/s 16ia only to the extent of **Rs 75,000**.” | Indicates that the deduction remains available even when the employee opts for the new tax regime, albeit with a higher ceiling. [C2] |

**Interpretation**

- The statutory provision (Section 16(ia)) expressly provides a **standard deduction** for any person whose income is chargeable under the head “Salaries” – i.e., salaried employees.  
- The amendment effective from 1 Oct 2024 sets the deduction at **₹ 50,000** (or salary, whichever is lower) for FY 2024‑25.  
- When the employee elects the **new tax regime (Section 115BAC)**, the same deduction is permissible, but the ceiling is **₹ 75,000** as per the validation rule for AY 2025‑26 (FY 2024‑25).  

Hence, a salaried employee can claim a standard deduction under Section 16(ia) in FY 2024‑25, subject to the applicable ceiling (₹ 50,000 in the old regime; up to ₹ 75,000 in the new regime).
